walkthroughs.body_html:
Thermodynamics — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Thermodynamics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Thermodynamics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which change has a positive entropy change?
options: Liquid water boiling to steam
Steam condensing to water
Water freezing to ice
Aqueous ions forming a solid precipitate

mcqs.q: A reaction is feasible at all temperatures when:
options: ΔH is negative and ΔS is positive
ΔH is positive and ΔS is negative
ΔH is negative and ΔS is negative
ΔH is positive and ΔS is positive

mcqs.q: The first ionisation energy of magnesium is the enthalpy change for:
options: Mg(g) → Mg⁺(g) + e⁻
Mg(s) → Mg⁺(g) + e⁻
Mg(g) → Mg²⁺(g) + 2e⁻
Mg(s) → Mg(g)

mcqs.q: The magnitude of lattice enthalpy is greatest when the ions are:
options: Small and highly charged
Large and singly charged
Large and highly charged
Small and uncharged

mcqs.q: Can an endothermic reaction ever be feasible?
options: It is endothermic because oxygen's nucleus is too heavy to attract electrons.
Yes — if TΔS outweighs ΔH so that ΔG is negative, as in many dissolving and decomposition processes at higher temperatures.
Endothermic reactions are feasible only below 0 °C.
Reactions only happen if they are exothermic.

mcqs.q: Why is the second electron affinity of oxygen endothermic?
options: The incoming electron is repelled by the already negative O⁻ ion, so energy must be supplied to force it on.
All electron affinities release energy because atoms 'want' a full outer shell.
It is endothermic because oxygen's nucleus is too heavy to attract electrons.
Endothermic reactions are feasible only below 0 °C.

mcqs.q: Does a negative ΔG mean the reaction will happen quickly?
options: It is endothermic because oxygen's nucleus is too heavy to attract electrons.
A thermodynamically feasible reaction always proceeds at a noticeable rate.
A negative ΔG means the reaction must be endothermic.
No — feasibility says nothing about rate; a feasible reaction can be immeasurably slow if its activation energy is high.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Lattice enthalpy of formation”?
options: The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous atoms is formed from an element in its standard state.
The enthalpy change when one mole of an ionic solid is formed from its gaseous ions; it is strongly exothermic.
ΔG = ΔH − TΔS combines enthalpy and entropy; a reaction is feasible when ΔG is zero or negative.
An energy cycle applying Hess's law to ionic compounds, used to calculate lattice enthalpies from measurable enthalpy changes.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “First electron affinity”?
options: An energy cycle applying Hess's law to ionic compounds, used to calculate lattice enthalpies from measurable enthalpy changes.
ΔG = ΔH − TΔS combines enthalpy and entropy; a reaction is feasible when ΔG is zero or negative.
The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous atoms each gain one electron to form 1− ions; exothermic for halogens.
The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous atoms is formed from an element in its standard state.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Born–Haber cycle”?
options: An energy cycle applying Hess's law to ionic compounds, used to calculate lattice enthalpies from measurable enthalpy changes.
A measure of disorder; entropy increases from solid to liquid to gas and when the number of gas molecules increases.
The enthalpy change when one mole of an ionic solid is formed from its gaseous ions; it is strongly exothermic.
ΔG = ΔH − TΔS combines enthalpy and entropy; a reaction is feasible when ΔG is zero or negative.

The enthalpy change when one mole of an ionic solid is formed from its gaseous ions; it is strongly exothermic.
ΔG = ΔH − TΔS combines enthalpy and entropy; a reaction is feasible when ΔG is zero or negative.
